paid_H1_remainder.claim: Source final chaos slack implies ||∇Y||_2²≤2000δ in addition to the stated ||Y||²≤1000δ.
paid_H1_remainder.derivation: For degree d≥2, retain k_d=1/500+(d/50)(1−2/d)(1+68/d). At d=2, k_d=d/1000. For d≥3, (1/50)(1−2/d)≥1/150>1/1000, so k_d≥d/1000. Source Dscript=−2δ is bounded by −Σ k_d||Y_d||²−Ω_B/1000. This uses paid proof operations, not a new source audit.

column_derivative_lemma.statement: For real symmetric H,L and slice matrices Xr with ΣXr²=B, (Σr||[Dq(H)−Dq(L)]Xr||F²)^(1/2)≤M sqrt(||B||op)||H−L||F, M=||Fourier(q second derivative)||L1 with consistent inversion normalization.
column_derivative_lemma.proof: Use q(z)=q(0)+q prime(0)z+∫hat(q second derivative)(t)(exp(itz)−1−itz)/(it)² dt. Twice differentiating the finite-matrix functional calculus gives two time-ordered Duhamel integrals. Their simplex volumes sum to1. Each integrand has form U E V Xr W or U Xr V E W with common unitaries U,V,W and E=H−L. Summed squared Frobenius norms over r are at most ||B||op||E||F² by trace cyclicity. Minkowski, followed by integration along L+sE, proves the claim. No factor from Σr||Xr||F² is introduced.
column_derivative_lemma.Fourier_condition: For inverse Gaussian Mills ratio q, q second and third derivatives belong to L2(R). Negative-tail derivatives are Gaussian-polynomial bounded since Φ(−a)≥1/2 for a≤0. For a→+∞ use Φ(−a)/φ(a)=a^−1∫_0∞exp(−u)exp(−u²/(2a²))du; dominated differentiation in w=1/a yields q(a)=a+a^−1−2a^−3+O(a^−5) with differentiated remainders, hence q second=O(a^−3), q third=O(a^−4). Plancherel and Cauchy–Schwarz with (1+t²)^−1 give Fourier(q second) in L1. Constants are absolute.
column_derivative_lemma.curl_application: A=L+Y, L=ΣxrXr, and q(A)=DF symmetric Jacobian. Matrix q is Frobenius1-Lipschitz, so ||Dq(A)[∇Y]||2≤||∇Y||2. Thus ||curl q(L)||2≤2(||∇Y||2+M sqrt(||B||op)||Y||2). For small absolute δ, paid Ω_B gives bounded B and this is O(sqrtδ).

opposite_input_symmetry_lemma.statement: Let T_rij=(Xr)_ij be real and symmetric in i,j, L(x)=ΣxrXr, B=ΣXr², K=||B||op. Define C_rij(x)=∂r q(L)_ij−∂i q(L)_rj and U_rij=T_rij−T_irj. For R²≥6K and c_R=min_[−R,R] q prime>0, ||U||F≤2||C||L2/c_R.
opposite_input_symmetry_lemma.pointwise_proof: At each x diagonalize L and rotate all three tensor indices. At −x the same basis diagonalizes −L. Set s=T_rij,t=T_irj, α=q[ai,aj],β=q[ar,aj], αprime=q[−ai,−aj],βprime=q[−ar,−aj]. The two curl entries are α(s−t)+(α−β)t and αprime(s−t)+(αprime−βprime)t. Convexity q second≥0 ensures the last coefficients have opposite signs. A convex combination therefore cancels t, with coefficient of s−t at least c_R when all three eigenvalues lie in [−R,R]. If both coefficients vanish, either equation suffices. Jensen gives |U_rij|²≤(C_rij(x)²+C_rij(−x)²)/c_R² on this triple spectral block. No eigenvector derivative is used.
opposite_input_symmetry_lemma.spectral_truncation: Write P_R for the spectral projection of L onto [−R,R]. Since U is a fixed tensor, E||(L acts on index j)U||²≤K||U||² for each of the three indices, using E L²=B. The union bound for commuting tensor-factor projections yields E||P_R^tensor3 U||²≥(1−3K/R²)||U||²≥||U||²/2. Integrating the pointwise bound and Gaussian symmetry proves the lemma.
opposite_input_symmetry_lemma.symmetrization: For a last-two-symmetric cubic T, its full orthogonal symmetrization S satisfies ||T−S||F²=||U||F²/3. Matrix row/column Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||B(S)−B(T)||F≤2sqrt(K)||T−S||F+||T−S||F². The preceding column derivative lemma transfers L2 curl to S at cost O(||T−S||F) when K is bounded.

strict_convexity_note: The source proves q second≥0 using survival submultiplicativity. Since q prime>0, S_a(u+v)<S_a(u)S_a(v) for u,v>0; integrating makes Var(Xa)<(E Xa)² and q second>0. Thus compact second-divided-difference weights are strictly positive for the author conditional symmetric-tensor commutator estimate.
